title: Which City Has the Most Michelin Stars? (2026 Rankings)
description: Tokyo has the most Michelin star restaurants of any city, France the most of any country. Every city, US city and country ranked, with what a star costs.
h1: The Cities and Countries With the Most Michelin Stars
summary: Every city, US city and country ranked by its starred restaurants and stars, with the price of a star in each.

body:
{{mostCity1}} has the most Michelin star restaurants of any city in the world: {{mostCity1N}}, holding {{mostCity1Stars}} stars between them, ahead of {{mostCity2}} ({{mostCity2N}}) and {{mostCity3}} ({{mostCity3N}}). {{topCountry}} has the most of any country, with {{topCountryN}}, and {{mostUS1}} leads US cities with {{mostUS1N}}.

These rankings count every restaurant starred in the current MICHELIN Guide editions, {{total}} in {{countries}} countries and territories, from the same list that powers The Starred Bill’s price pages, and they are rebuilt whenever a guide changes. Because we also know what each restaurant charges, every table adds what a star costs: the typical dinner tasting menu and the price per star, in US dollars. New to the stars? Start with what a Michelin star means.

What city has the most Michelin star restaurants?

{{mostCity1}}, by a distance. Its {{mostCity1N}} starred restaurants split into {{mostCity1Split}}, and on its own the city has more starred restaurants than {{mostCityBeats}} of the {{countries}} countries and territories in the guide. {{mostCity2}} is second with {{mostCity2N}}, then {{mostCity3}} ({{mostCity3N}}), {{mostCity4}} ({{mostCity4N}}) and {{mostCity5}} ({{mostCity5N}}). In all, {{mostCities10}} cities have ten or more.

{{table:most-cities}}

Japan’s hold on the top of the list is the striking thing. Three of the five most starred cities are Japanese, and Nara, a small city of temples and deer an hour from Osaka, has {{inCity_nara}} starred restaurants, about as many as Rome ({{inCity_rome}}). Japanese restaurants tend to be small and specialized: an eight-seat sushi counter, a tempura bar, a kaiseki house with a handful of private rooms. A city full of tiny, focused kitchens gives inspectors far more to star than one built around big dining rooms. When the MICHELIN Guide first came to Tokyo in November 2007, it awarded 191 stars to 150 restaurants, more stars than Paris held at the time, and Tokyo has topped the count ever since.

Paris and London are the only European cities in the top ten. The rest of France’s {{topCountryN}} starred restaurants are spread across the country, in regional cities such as Lyon and in villages with a single starred inn, which is why France leads the countries with only one city near the top.

Which city has the most Michelin stars?

Count stars rather than restaurants, so that a three-star restaurant counts three, and {{mostStarsCity}} still leads, with {{mostStarsCityN}}. It also has the most three-star restaurants, {{most3CityN}}, ahead of {{most3City2}} with {{most3City2N}}. Sort the table by “Total stars” and cities with several two- and three-star restaurants, such as Hong Kong and San Francisco, climb past those whose stars are mostly single ones.

What a Michelin star costs, city by city

This is where our prices come in. Divide each restaurant’s dinner tasting menu by its stars and the median comes to {{mostPerStar}} per star worldwide. Among the cities in the table, a star is cheapest in {{mostCheapStar}}, at about {{mostCheapStarUSD}}, and dearest in {{mostDearStar}}, at about {{mostDearStarUSD}}. Copenhagen looks expensive partly because Danish menu prices already include service and 25% VAT, which most countries add on top.

Japan, Taiwan and Thailand are where stars come cheapest. A star costs about {{perStar_bangkok}} in Bangkok, {{perStar_taipei}} in Taipei and {{perStar_osaka}} in Osaka, against {{perStar_paris}} in Paris, {{perStar_new_york}} in New York and {{perStar_los_angeles}} in Los Angeles. A typical tasting menu in New York costs {{menu_new_york}} before tax and tip; in Tokyo it is {{menu_tokyo}}. Mainland Chinese cities are blank in the price columns, because their restaurants rarely publish a set menu price; our pages list what a meal there typically costs instead.

The price per star is a median, so every city has restaurants well below it, especially at lunch. For the cheapest single meals, from noodle counters to set lunches, see the cheapest Michelin star meals in the world.

US cities with the most Michelin star restaurants

{{mostUS1}} has the most Michelin star restaurants in the US, {{mostUS1N}} across its five boroughs, {{mostUS13}} of them with three stars. {{mostUS2}} ({{mostUS2N}}) and {{mostUS3}} ({{mostUS3N}}) come next, then {{mostUS4}} ({{mostUS4N}}).

{{table:most-us-cities}}

The MICHELIN Guide covers only parts of the US, state by state, so a food city outside its guides has no stars, however good its restaurants. The San Francisco figure counts the city alone: the wine country and the rest of the Bay Area, from Healdsburg to the Napa Valley, are on our California page. By state, {{topState}} leads with {{topStateN}} starred restaurants, ahead of {{secondState}} with {{secondStateN}}.

Which country has the most Michelin star restaurants?

{{topCountry}} is the country with the most Michelin star restaurants: {{topCountryN}}, holding {{mostCountryStars}} stars, more than any other country by either count. {{top3Country}} also has the most three-star restaurants, {{top3N}}, ahead of {{second3Country}} with {{second3N}}. {{secondCountry}} is second by restaurants, with {{secondCountryN}}, but count stars and {{mostStarsCountry2}} moves ahead: it has {{mostStarsCountry2N}} stars to {{mostStarsCountry3}}’s {{mostStarsCountry3N}}, because more of its restaurants hold two or three.

{{table:most-countries}}

Europe fills most of the top places because the guide began in France in 1900 and spread through Europe long before it reached New York in 2005 and Tokyo in 2007. For every country and US state, including those with only one or two starred restaurants, see how many Michelin star restaurants each country has.

Which country has the most Michelin stars per person?

{{mostPer1}}, among countries of a million people or more: it has {{mostPer1N}} starred restaurants for every million people, ahead of {{mostPer2}} ({{mostPer2N}}) and {{mostPer3}} ({{mostPer3N}}). France has {{perM_france}}, the UK {{perM_uk}} and the US {{perM_usa}}.

{{table:most-per-person}}

The smallest places beat them all. Monaco has {{in_monaco}} starred restaurants for about 38,000 people, Macau {{in_macau}} for fewer than 700,000, many of them in its casino resorts, and Luxembourg {{in_luxembourg}} for about 670,000.

Big food cities with no Michelin stars

Some of the world’s great eating cities are missing from these tables because the MICHELIN Guide has never covered them. Sydney and Melbourne have no stars, although Michelin’s first Australian guide, for South Australia, reveals its stars on 14 October 2026, as our guide to Michelin star restaurants in Australia explains. Mumbai and Delhi have none because there is no guide for India yet, which our page on Michelin stars and India follows, and Cape Town has none for the same reason, as our guide to Michelin star restaurants in South Africa explains.

How we count

Stars come only from the MICHELIN Guide, from the current edition for each country and territory; restaurants that have closed or lost their stars are left out. Each city counts the restaurants on our page for it, so boroughs and districts count under their city, while nearby towns count on their own: Yountville is not part of San Francisco, nor Bray part of London. Prices are each restaurant’s main dinner tasting menu, per person before service and drinks, converted to US dollars at recent exchange rates. Figures last checked {{checked}}.

Using these figures? Please credit The Starred Bill and link to this page; the tables update whenever a MICHELIN Guide edition changes.

faq.q: Which restaurant has the most Michelin stars?
faq.a: No restaurant can have more than three Michelin stars, the guide’s highest award, and {{n3}} restaurants hold three today. Chefs can hold more by running several restaurants: among living chefs, {{nameLiving}}’s {{nameLivingN}} restaurants hold {{nameLivingStars}} stars between them.

faq.q: How many cities have Michelin star restaurants?
faq.a: {{mostCities}} towns and cities have at least one starred restaurant, and {{mostCities10}} have ten or more. Many of the rest are villages and country towns, especially in France, Italy and Germany, with a single starred restaurant or inn.

faq.q: Does London or Paris have more Michelin stars?
faq.a: Paris, with {{inCity_paris}} starred restaurants to London’s {{inCity_london}}, and Paris has more three-star restaurants too. Both are well behind Tokyo, and Kyoto, a city of under 1.5 million people, has {{inCity_kyoto}}.
